header.contentDescription: An aerofoil at ten degrees with tracer dots running the streamlines, faster where the flow crowds above the wing

drawTextAnchored.text: crowded above — faster air, lower pressure
spread below — slower air, higher pressure
and it all leaves pointing down
The wing turns air downward and lift is the reaction to that. Pressure difference and
downwash are two descriptions of one event, not two causes. Past about 15° the flow over
the top separates and lift collapses — a stall is an angle, not a speed.
watch the dots overtake above the wing
